title: Cluster Chronicle: consolidated timeline and rollback slate for private console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a consolidated Cluster Chronicle view for the Private/VPC console that combines event timeline, per-tenant status, cost impact preview, and an actionable rollback slate. The goal is to enable operators and owners to quickly understand a cluster's recent changes (upgrades, config patches, network events), evaluate fallout across tenants, and stage safe rollbacks or mitigations without leaving the console.
context_and_goals: Operators managing private clusters need a single surface that reduces cognitive load during incidents and routine upgrades. Current status pages and upgrade flows are fragmented across the console. Chronicle should surface causality (what change likely caused the degradation), a time-ordered event stream, quick filters (by tenant, firmware/agent version, region), a cost delta estimator for rollback vs forward fix, and an unobtrusive safety check system for staged rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Single chronologically-ordered timeline with event types (upgrade, config change, autoscale, network flap, fallback) and expandable details
Per-event impact map showing affected tenants and tenant-level health summaries
Rollback slate: pre-approved rollback actions with required confirmations and safety checks (canary filters, quota checks)
Cost impact preview: rough estimate (tokens/min or $/hour) for rollback vs continued degraded service
Prototype accessible in Figma with interactive microflows for selection, preview, and commit
Cross-links to relevant GitHub PRs, runbooks, and dashboards included in event details
Keyboard accessible timeline navigation and screen-reader friendly labels
design_notes: We intentionally group events by causal clusters (heuristic based on time window + overlapping tenant impact). Timeline lanes: control-plane events, infra events, network events, tenant-config changes. Each event card has: timestamp, actor (human/automation), short summary, affected tenant count, severity tag, links to artifacts. Rollback slate is not a separate modal but a slide-over anchored to the event card to preserve context and reduce mental model switching.
engineering_feedback: ENG input (2025-02-12): prefer server-side aggregation for causal clustering; frontend should request condensed event buckets for performance
ENG note (2025-02-14): rollback slate needs to call the rollout API with a dry-run option; add explicit idempotency token in API contract
Infra (2025-02-15): timeline queries must be paginated and limited to a 90-day window to avoid heavy queries on large clusters
accessibility_considerations: Timeline must support linear reading order, ARIA roles for event cards and slide-over actions, visible focus states for all interactive controls, and color-defensive severity indicators (icons + labels).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Embedding rollback actions in the timeline reduces context switches but increases the chances of accidental commits; mitigations: require multi-step confirmation, show canary scope, require two approvals for high-severity tenant-impacting rollbacks, and add a 30s grace period with cancel option. Cost estimator accuracy will be intentionally coarse +/- 20% to avoid overpromising.
review_notes: PM review (2025-02-16, Maya Rivera): likes consolidated surface; asked for clearer tenant ownership badges and link to billing owner
SRE review (2025-02-17, Davinder Singh): approved causal grouping heuristic but requested a "confidence" indicator per group
Security review (2025-02-18, Priya Nair): flagged RBAC checks for rollback actions; design updated to grey out actions when user lacks permission and surface why
decisions: Use slide-over anchored to event card for rollback slate instead of full modal
Server-side causal clustering with confidence score returned to UI
Show cost delta as a relative band with min/median/max values
Require canary definition when rollback affects >5 tenants
next_steps: Address ENG API contract: add dry-run and idempotency fields (owner: Jonah)
Finalize Figma micro-interactions and handoff tokens for CSS vars (owner: Aisha)
Create a lightweight usability test with 6 SREs and 4 platform engineers (target: 2025-02-25)
